Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right lower lung, with the follow-up image (Figure 4), there is clear progression with increased density in the right lung and the appearance of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal consolidation in a patient with subacute symptoms unresponsive to antibiotics is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma).
